notes: OpenZeppelin AccessManager. All small views reviewed in detail; the restricted setters, execute, schedule, cancel, consumeScheduledOp by structure (prologue of onlyAuthorized with its three paths: self-call with the transient execution id, immediate, delayed via a scheduled op). Source loops: 2, whiles: setTargetFunctionRole's for (printed 3 times, once per path of the onlyAuthorized prologue, P12: 1578, 1698, 1749) and Multicall's for (241; the pack has no AST source for multicall, but OZ Multicall has the loop). Implicit loops: multicall's rotated zero-init of new bytes[](n) ('while idx - 1', P3) and its return encoding. P12: the whole body of setTargetFunctionRole and of the other restricted functions repeated in each authorization path (~60 lines). The transient execution id prints as transient[-4] (TransientSlot at keccak-derived slot).
summary: Faithful, with both loops found; readability suffers from the restricted-function bodies repeated per authorization path, the allowedRoles mapping-in-struct left as raw keccak arithmetic, and the operation id recomputed on every line.
